content_units: Best Fit for a 2-Person Cape Town Household

For one person on work video calls and another streaming 4K at night,   fiber is the safer choice   and   Plan A is the best 12-month value   for most households. It gives enough speed for both users, includes the router, and has the lowest first-year cost among the fiber options.
12-Month Value Comparison
Plan   Type   Speed   Contract   12-Month Cost   Key Tradeoff
A   Fiber uncapped   50/25 Mbps   12 months     R8,388     Locked in for a year
B   Fiber uncapped   100/50 Mbps   Month-to-month     R11,988 + R1,200 = R13,188     Much higher first-year cost
C   Fixed LTE   30/10 Mbps   Month-to-month     R6,588     500 GB fair use; less stable than fiber
Recommendation
Best value: Plan A
-   Why it wins:   50/25 Mbps is usually enough for a home office video caller plus a 4K stream at the same time.
-   Cost advantage:   It saves   R4,800   vs Plan B over 12 months.
-   Better fit than LTE:   More stable latency and consistency than fixed LTE for work calls.
When Plan B is worth it
If the work-from-home person does frequent large uploads, cloud backups, or if both people are often online heavily at the same time,   Plan B   is the smoother premium option.
- Upload is   50 Mbps vs 25 Mbps   on Plan A.
- Month-to-month flexibility is valuable if you may move or cancel soon.
- But you are paying a large premium for that flexibility and extra headroom.
Why Plan C is the risky choice
-   30/10 Mbps   can be tight for HD/4K streaming plus video calls, especially during peak mobile-network congestion.
-   500 GB fair use   is the biggest hidden risk:
- 4K streaming can consume a lot of data over a month.
- Heavy nightly streaming could push usage toward fair-use thresholds.
- LTE latency and tower congestion can hurt call quality more than fiber.
Hidden Tradeoffs to Watch
Plan A: lower price, lower flexibility
- 12-month contract may include cancellation penalties if you leave early.
- 25 Mbps upload is fine for calls, but less ideal for frequent large file uploads.
Plan B: flexibility costs money
- Router adds   R1,200 once-off  , increasing real first-year spend.
- Best if flexibility matters or you want more future-proof speed.
Plan C: cheapest monthly price, but not cheapest risk
- Fair-use policy may reduce performance or create service-management issues after high usage.
- Fixed LTE performance can vary by area, signal strength, and evening congestion.
